record.paper_title: Relativistic jets in narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies. New discoveries and open questions
record.original_question: In active galactic nuclei, accretion of gas onto a super-massive black hole is thought to power a relativistic jet that is roughly perpendicular to the accretion disk. What is the nature of the coupling between the accretion disk and the relativistic jet that allows some active galactic nuclei to launch these highly collimated, high-energy outflows?

evidence.quote: Accretion of gas onto the super-massive black hole (SMBH) is thought to power these collimated jets, even if the nature of the coupling between the accretion disk and the jet is still among the outstanding open questions in high-energy astrophysics

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider an active galactic nucleus consisting of a super-massive black hole of mass $M \gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$ surrounded by an accretion disk of ionized gas, from which a relativistic, highly collimated bipolar jet is launched approximately perpendicular to the disk plane. Treating the disk as a magnetized plasma flow governed by general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamics around a (possibly rotating) Kerr black hole, determine the physical mechanism that couples the accretion disk to the relativistic jet and is responsible for jet launching, collimation, and acceleration. In particular, identify which of the proposed coupling mechanisms — for instance, magnetic extraction of black-hole rotational energy via large-scale poloidal magnetic fields threading the horizon (Blandford–Znajek-type processes), magneto-centrifugal acceleration of disk material along open field lines anchored in the disk (Blandford–Payne-type processes), or radiation/thermal pressure driving — operates, and characterize the conditions on accretion rate, black-hole spin, magnetic flux, and disk structure under which a powerful relativistic jet can be produced.
artifact.status_search_result: The precise physical mechanism coupling accretion disks to relativistic jets in AGN remains an open problem in high-energy astrophysics. While candidate mechanisms (Blandford–Znajek, Blandford–Payne, magnetically arrested disks) are well studied via GRMHD simulations and observational correlations (e.g., between black-hole spin, magnetic flux, and jet power), no consensus, fully predictive theory of disk–jet coupling has been established as of recent reviews.
